title: stabilize constrained-sampling integration and tool-framing for OpenAI-compat streaming
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers reported intermittent failures when using constrained structured-output (CFG/regex) together with streaming responses and OpenAI-compatible tool/function calling. Failures took two forms: (1) partial tool-call tokens emitted mid-stream caused downstream tool parsers to error, and (2) heavy batching could cause constraint state to be dropped leading to invalid outputs. This PR unifies the sampling boundary between constrained backends and the serving runtime, adds tokenizer-aware anchoring for regex constraints, and introduces a small framing shim so OpenAI-compat streaming emits tool-call markers atomically. The changes are primarily runtime-facing: a new ConstraintSampler interface that formalizes lookahead scoring, updated grammar and regex backends to respect token boundaries, stronger backpressure for streaming so a partial token is never flushed, and a compatibility shim that tags function-call start/end as single logical events for clients. Also includes new unit/integration tests and a small perf micro-benchmark.
commits: feat(constraints): introduce ConstraintSampler trait and common sampling helpers
fix(regex): tokenizer-aware anchoring to prevent partial-match emission during streaming
feat(grammar): deterministic lookahead scoring to prioritize CFG-safe prefix completions
chore(compat): OpenAI streaming shim emits tool_call_start/tool_call_end events (atomic framing)
test: add end-to-end test for function-calling with constrained outputs and streaming
perf: add micro-benchmark and reduce lock contention in constraint evaluation path
review_thread: Arjun Patel: The design doc helps — can you clarify how batching interacts with deterministic lookahead? Would prefer an explicit safety net if lookahead fails under timeout.
Maya Chen: Added a fallthrough that uses conservative sampling (reject partial token) and a 10ms timeout before reverting to conservative behavior. Documented in remarks and tests.
Lucia Gomez: Tests look solid; can you add a quick benchmark showing latency impact at p99 with and without the framing shim?
Maya Chen: Added micro-benchmark in benchmarks/constraints and included summary numbers in the PR description. Impact at p99 is +1.8ms on a 2048-seq worst-case; acceptable given correctness gains.
Evan Park: One nit: rename tool_call_{start,end} to tool_call_event.{start,end} so it reads better in logs. Otherwise LGTM.
Maya Chen: Renamed events and updated consumers. Thanks.
Arjun Patel: Approving — verified the e2e test locally against a busy serving node and observed no partial-tool tokens.
merge_commit_message:
stabilize constrained-sampling integration and tool framing for openai-compat streaming

Introduces ConstraintSampler, tokenizer-aware regex anchoring, deterministic grammar lookahead, and atomic tool-call framing for streaming. Adds tests and a perf micro-benchmark.
release_notes: Fixes intermittent tool/function-calling failures when using constrained structured outputs with streaming. Adds tokenizer-aware regex anchoring, a unified ConstraintSampler interface, and atomic tool-call framing for OpenAI-compat streams. No API breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Deploy on serving nodes sequentially (canary -> ramp) because the new sampling code changes lock contention observed in micro-benchmarks. CI pipeline adds an integration job that must pass before rollout. If rollbacks are needed, revert the feature branch on the canary pool first.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for sampler edge cases, integration tests that exercise streaming + function calling, and an e2e reproduction harness used during triage of SUP-872. All new tests added to CI pipeline and passed on the merged commit.
notes: This PR intentionally favors correctness over a very small latency increase at p99 for constrained workloads. We may explore incremental optimizations (lock-free scoring cache) in follow-ups.
